label: Letters j/f/i/s/b/g/a input early in the original sequence or as its last token
explanation: Token-selective unit that fires during the original-input phase (96% of activation mass). Almost all of it comes when the input is one of j, f, i, s, b, g, a; j and f are the strongest (about 22% of the mass each, around 25% firing rate), and g and a are weaker and mostly fire at t=0. Position strongly modulates firing: the rate is highest at t=0 (23%) and falls through t=1-2, then rises again at the last original positions of long sequences (orig_idx 7-8). The largest activations are on j/f as the last original token (to_go=0), often followed by weak-to-moderate firing on <DEL>. It mostly fires on first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 95% of the mass), and its rate drops when other set tokens have already appeared. It is essentially silent in the copy phase, and it fires weakly on n/z/0/c, mostly at the first step. On dev the predicate gives F1 ~0.60 and mass recall ~0.76. Even with the right token at the right position the unit often does not fire, which suggests it depends on hidden state that the variables here do not capture.
